§ 3EARTH'S INTERIOR

Four Methods to Know About Earth's Interior

  1. 1. Temperature: Indirect source.
  2. 2. Volcanoes: Direct source.
  3. 3. Rocks: Direct source.
  4. 4. Meteorites: Indirect source.
  5. 5. Earthquake: Indirect source.
Father of Geology: James Hutton

Layers of Earth

#### Crust

  • It is made of Silica and Aluminium layer (SiAl).
  • Thickness: 5–70 km.
  • Crust has two divisions:
Continental CrustOceanic Crust
It is the land part of the crust, the outermost layer of the Earth that makes up the continents and continental shelvesIt is the water part of the crust, the solid layer Earth's crust that lies beneath the ocean.
It is thick (30 km)It is thin (5 km)
It is lighterIt is denser
It is made of granitic rockIt is made of Basaltic rock.
  • Granite is found in Continental crust.
  • Basalt is found in Oceanic crust.

#### Mantle

  • It is made of Silica and Magnesium (SiMa).
  • Thickness: 2900 km.
  • Mantle has two divisions: Upper Mantle and Lower Mantle.
  • Asthenosphere: It is a semi-solid/semi-molten layer of earth's upper mantle that is mechanically weak, and ductile. It lies beneath the lithosphere (the rigid outermost layer of earth made up of crust and upper solid mantle with 10–200 km of thickness). Asthenosphere is a source of magma/lava.
Asthenosphere is not a part of Lithosphere.

#### Core

  • It is made of Nickel and Iron (NiFe).
  • Core has two divisions:
  1. 1. Inner core: It is in solid form (2200 km).
  2. 2. Outer core: It is in liquid form and shows magnetic properties (1300 km).
ByCrustMantleCore
Volume1%84%15%
Mass1%68%31%

Earth's Discontinuity

  • Conrad discontinuity — between upper & lower crust
  • Mohorovicic discontinuity — between lower crust & upper mantle
  • Repetti discontinuity — between upper & lower Mantle
  • Guttenberg discontinuity — between lower Mantle & outer Core
  • Lehmann discontinuity — between outer & inner Core
TRICK TO REMEMBER: Conrad → Koi, Mohorovicic → Mujhe, Repetti → Red, Guttenberg → Gulab, Lehmann → Lado — Koi Mujhe Red Gulab Lado

§ 4Force of Drifting

  • Theory of Plate Tectonics: It is given McKenzie and Parker in 1967. This theory suggests that the Earth's lithosphere (crust and uppermost mantle) is broken into large, rigid plates that move and interact with each other, driving various geological phenomena.
  • Convection Current Theory: It is given by Arthur Holmes. Holmes theorised that convection currents move through the mantle, the same way heated air circulates through a room and radically reshape the Earth's surface in the process.

§ 5Earthquake

  • An earthquake is an intense shaking of Earth's surface, which caused due to shifting of Earth's plate. It is a sudden release of energy along the fall line in the form of waves (also known as seismic waves).
  • Epicentre: It is the point on the Earth's surface directly above the earthquake's focus (also known as the hypocentre), where the earthquake originates underground.
  • Hypocentre: It is the point within the Earth where the earthquake begins.
  • All natural earthquake occur in lithosphere.
  • Earthquake generate seismic waves, which are vibrations that travel through the earth in the form of body waves and surface waves.

Body Waves

  • These waves travel through the Earth's interior with high speed.
  • They are of two types: P-waves and S-waves.
P-wavesS-waves
They are also known as primary wavesThey are also known as secondary waves
They are the fastest seismic waves (first to record on seismograph) → 7–8 km/secThey are the slow seismic waves in-comparison to P-waves → 4–6 km/sec
They can travel through all medium (solid > liquid > gas)They can travel through only solids
P-waves are longitudinal compression waves, similar to sound wavesS-waves are transverse waves, that causes the ground to vibrate perpendicular to the direction of the wave
They create compression and rarefaction and also causes stretching and squeezingThey create crest and trough
Note: Shallow focus, earthquakes have more intensity than the deeper ones.

Surface Waves

  • When body waves come in contact with surface rocks, they form surface waves.
  • They are more destructive in nature.
  • Rayleigh waves / Love waves (L-waves) are types of surface waves.
  • They are the last to record on seismograph.
A seismograph is an instrument that measures and registers seismic waves that travel through the Earth as the outcome of an earthquake.

Scales to Measure Earthquake

Richter ScaleMercalli Scale
It is an instrument to measure magnitude of the earthquakeIt is an instrument to measure the intensity of the earthquake
It measures magnitude from 0 to 10It measures intensity from 1 to 12
It is a limitless scale

Shadow Zone of Waves

  • The shadow zone of an earthquake is the area of the Earth, where certain seismic waves are not detected. The shadow zone of S-waves is larger than the shadow zone of P-waves.

Effects of Earthquake

  • Tsunami (Japanese term): These are harbour waves. It occurs when earthquake occur, occurs at sea floor.
  • Soil liquefaction
  • Landslide
  • Avalanche
  • Floods
  • Fire

Types of Earthquake

  • Collapse earthquake: These are small earthquake that occurs when the roof of underground mine or caverns collapse.
  • Explosion earthquake: An earthquake caused by detonation of a chemical or nuclear device.
  • Tectonic earthquake: An earthquake caused by movement of earth's tectonic plates.
  • Reservoir induced earthquake: An occurrence of earthquakes caused by construction of large reservoirs. This is human-induced earthquake.
  • Volcanic earthquake: An earthquake that occurs as result of volcanic eruption.

Earthquake Zones of India

Earthquake caused in BHUJ (Gujarat) in 2001 with a magnitude of 7.7

  • Zone V (highest)
  • Zone IV
  • Zone III
  • Zone II (least active)

§ 6Tectonic Plates

  • Lithosphere makes plates comprising crust and upper solid part of Mantle.
  • There are 7 major + few minor plates.
Major Tectonic PlatesMinor Tectonic Plates
Pacific plateCocos plate
North American plateNazca plate
South American plateCaribbean plate
African plateIndian plate
Antarctic platePhilippine plate
Eurasian plate
Australian plate

Ring of Fire

  • It is a result of plate tectonics. It is a horse-shoe-shaped region around the Pacific Ocean. It is a high earthquake and volcano prone region.
  • Volcano: 75%; Earthquake: 90%
  • Convection current that occurs in the asthenosphere is the force behind the plate movement. The heat from the Earth's interior causes currents of hot rising magma and cooler sinking magma to flow, moving the lithospheric plates along with them.

Three Types of Plate Boundary

DivergentConvergentTransform
Occurs when two tectonic plates move away from each other, causes lava to explode, leading to new crust formationIt happens when plates collide, causing one plate to subduct beneath the other creating a subduction zone, potentially destroying the crustIt is a plate boundary where plates slide pass each other horizontally, neither creating nor destroying crust

§ 7Key concepts

  • Methods to know Earth's interior: Temperature & Earthquake (indirect), Volcanoes & Rocks (direct). Father of Geology = James Hutton.
  • Crust — SiAl (Silica + Aluminium), 5–70 km thick; Continental = thick (30 km), light, granitic; Oceanic = thin (5 km), dense, basaltic.
  • Mantle — SiMa (Silica + Magnesium), 2900 km thick; Upper & Lower divisions. Asthenosphere = semi-solid/semi-molten upper mantle beneath lithosphere, source of magma/lava; NOT part of lithosphere.
  • Core — NiFe (Nickel + Iron); Inner core = solid (2200 km); Outer core = liquid, magnetic (1300 km).
  • Volume %: Crust 1 / Mantle 84 / Core 15. Mass %: Crust 1 / Mantle 68 / Core 31.
  • Discontinuities (top → bottom): Conrad (upper/lower crust), Mohorovicic (lower crust/upper mantle), Repetti (upper/lower mantle), Guttenberg (lower mantle/outer core), Lehmann (outer/inner core). Trick: Koi Mujhe Red Gulab Lado.
  • Theory of Plate Tectonics (McKenzie & Parker, 1967) — lithosphere broken into rigid plates that move and interact. Convection Current Theory (Arthur Holmes) — convection currents in mantle drive plate motion.
  • Earthquake — sudden release of energy along a fault from shifting of plates → seismic waves. Epicentre = surface point above focus. Hypocentre/Focus = underground point where earthquake begins. All natural earthquakes occur in lithosphere.
  • Body waves travel through Earth's interior. P-waves = primary, fastest (7–8 km/s), longitudinal, all media. S-waves = secondary, slower (4–6 km/s), transverse, solids only. Shallow-focus earthquakes are more intense than deeper ones.
  • Surface waves — formed when body waves hit surface rocks; more destructive; Rayleigh & Love (L-)waves; last to record.
  • Seismograph — instrument that measures and registers seismic waves.
  • Richter Scale measures magnitude 0–10 (limitless). Mercalli Scale measures intensity 1–12.
  • Shadow zone — area where seismic waves are not detected. S-wave shadow zone is larger than P-wave shadow zone (because outer core is liquid; S-waves don't travel through liquid). S-wave shadow zone = 40% of Earth's surface.
  • Earthquake effects: Tsunami (harbour waves, at sea floor), soil liquefaction, landslide, avalanche, floods, fire.
  • Earthquake types: Collapse (mine/cavern roof), Explosion (chemical/nuclear device), Tectonic (plate movement), Reservoir-induced (large reservoirs; human-induced), Volcanic (volcanic eruption).
  • Indian earthquake zones: Zone V (highest), IV, III, II (least active). 2001 Bhuj (Gujarat) earthquake = magnitude 7.7.
  • Tectonic plates — lithosphere broken into 7 major + few minor. Major: Pacific, North American, South American, African, Antarctic, Eurasian, Australian. Minor: Cocos, Nazca, Caribbean, Indian, Philippine.
  • Ring of Fire — horse-shoe-shaped region around Pacific Ocean; result of plate tectonics; high earthquake (90%) & volcano (75%) prone zone.
  • Plate boundaries:
  • Divergent — plates move apart → lava explodes → new crust formed.
  • Convergent — plates collide → one subducts → subduction zone → destroys crust.
  • Transform — plates slide past each other horizontally → neither creates nor destroys crust.
